title: Alpha tags versus merge gates
summary: In Sovereign Core, merging and Alpha tagging are separate. GitHub has no GB10, so its thin gate checks a signed bundle for the changed scope. An Alpha is a main commit judged in full scope, and verify-bundle --require-full rejects it with NOT_FULL_SCOPE or NO_GPU_RECEIPT unless a required gb10 check ran on the Spark's GPU. The first Alpha was 34 host checks, which is why the rule exists. I can show you a teaching model of those rules in Omega.
goal: Tell the merge gate from the Alpha gate, and see why all-green host checks are not an Alpha without a GPU receipt.
key_steps: Merging: the changed-scope bundle must PASS; usually host-only
Alpha: the main commit is judged in full scope, every gate
Require a gb10 check that actually ran: PASS or FAIL counts, a self NOT_RUN does not
Never reuse a GPU result across commits
Remember an Alpha is still not hardware QUALIFIED

example.code:
note alphachk: a teaching model of the Alpha rule in aien-test verify-bundle --require-full (not that tool)
note input lines: "scope full|changed" and "check NAME BACKEND VERDICT", BACKEND host|gb10, VERDICT PASS|FAIL|NOT_RUN
note rules, in order: malformed input REFUSED; scope not full REJECTED NOT_FULL_SCOPE; any FAIL is FAIL (a gb10
note FAIL is still a receipt); no gb10 check that ran REJECTED NO_GPU_RECEIPT; any NOT_RUN is NOT_RUN; else ALPHA
note exit 0 ALPHA, 1 FAIL, 2 NOT_RUN, 3 REJECTED, 4 REFUSED
text words "scope check full changed host gb10 PASS FAIL NOT_RUN "
text tby "checks by backend: host="
text tgpu " gb10="
text tran "gb10 checks that ran (PASS or FAIL): "
text vok "verdict ALPHA: full-scope PASS that carries a gb10 receipt\n"
text vfail "verdict FAIL\n"
text vnrun "verdict NOT_RUN\n"
text vscope "verdict REJECTED NOT_FULL_SCOPE: plan scope is not full\n"
text vgpu "verdict REJECTED NO_GPU_RECEIPT: no required gb10 check ran on the GPU\n"
text vref "verdict REFUSED malformed line\n"
text nl "\n"
note g: 0 scope (1 full, 2 changed), 1 host, 2 gb10, 3 gb10 ran, 4 fails, 5 not run, 6 malformed
global g ulong 7
fn bump i ulong to void
put g i add get g i 1
end
fn tok a ulong b ulong to long
note the word a .. b-1 as an index into words
ret lookup words a b
end
fn check a ulong b ulong to void
note a is just after "check "; skip NAME, then read BACKEND and VERDICT
e = wordend a b
if ge e b
bump 6
else
p = add e 1
e = wordend p b
be = tok p e
if ge e b
bump 6
else
v = tok add e 1 b
if eq be 4
bump 1
else
if eq be 5
bump 2
else
bump 6
end
end
if eq v 7
bump 4
end
if eq v 8
bump 5
end
if lt v 6
bump 6
end
if eq be 5
if or eq v 6 eq v 7
bump 3
end
end
end
end
end
fn oneline a ulong b ulong to void
if lt a b
e = wordend a b
w = tok a e
if ge e b
bump 6
else
if eq w 0
s = tok add e 1 b
if eq s 2
put g 0 1
else
if eq s 3
put g 0 2
else
bump 6
end
end
else
if eq w 1
check add e 1 b
else
bump 6
end
end
end
end
end
fn verdict to int
if gt get g 6 0
ot vref
ret 4
end
if ne get g 0 1
ot vscope
ret 3
end
if gt get g 4 0
ot vfail
ret 1
end
if eq get g 3 0
ot vgpu
ret 3
end
if gt get g 5 0
ot vnrun
ret 2
end
ot vok
ret 0
end
fn main to int
r = rdall
if lt r 0
ret 4
end
if eq get st 2 1
ret 4
end
n = ulong r
a = ulong 0
for i ulong n
if eq get inb i 10
oneline a i
a = add i 1
end
end
oneline a n
ot tby
on get g 1
ot tgpu
on get g 2
ot nl
ot tran
on get g 3
ot nl
v = verdict
f = flush
ret v
end

REJECTED NO_GPU_RECEIPT: an Alpha needs a required check on backend gb10 that ran on the Spark's GPU, and this full-scope bundle has none (checks by backend: host=34; gb10 checks: none)
every verdict as expected: yes

common_mistake: Treating 'all checks green' as release-ready without asking which scope and which backend. A green changed-scope PR is mergeable, not an Alpha; an Alpha is one GPU run, not hardware qualification.
